question: An inverting amplifier uses Rin = 4.7 kOhm and Rf = 47 kOhm with an ideal op-amp. The input is 0.5 V DC. Find the output voltage.
A non-inverting amplifier has R1 = 2 kOhm from the inverting input to ground and Rf = 18 kOhm from the output to the inverting input. The input is 0.3 V. Find the output voltage.
An inverting summing amplifier has Rf = 10 kOhm and three inputs: V1 = 2 V through 10 kOhm, V2 = -1 V through 5 kOhm and V3 = 0.5 V through 20 kOhm. Find the output voltage.

A difference amplifier has R1 = 10 kOhm from V2 to the inverting input, R2 = 50 kOhm from the inverting input to the output, R3 = 10 kOhm from V1 to the non-inverting input and R4 = 50 kOhm from the non-inverting input to ground. V1 = 1.2 V and V2 = 1.0 V. Find the output voltage.
A voltage follower is driven by a 2.5 V source and drives a 250 Ohm load. Find the output voltage and the current the op-amp supplies to the load.
An inverting amplifier has Rin = 2.2 kOhm and Rf = 22 kOhm. Find its voltage gain and its input resistance.
work: gain = -22k/2.2k = -10; Rin = 2.2k (inverting input is a virtual ground)

question: A non-inverting amplifier has R1 = 1 kOhm to ground and Rf = 99 kOhm. The op-amp has a finite open-loop gain A0 = 10^4. The input is 10 mV DC. Find the output voltage.
A non-inverting amplifier with R1 = 1 kOhm and Rf = 19 kOhm uses an op-amp with A0 = 200000 and GBW = 1 MHz. Find the closed-loop -3 dB bandwidth.
A non-inverting amplifier has R1 = 1 kOhm and Rf = 10 kOhm and is powered from +/-12 V supplies. The input is 1.5 V DC. Find the output voltage.
work: linear 11*1.5 = 16.5 V > 12 V rail -> saturation warning

question: An op-amp integrator has R = 10 kOhm from the input to the inverting input and C = 10 nF from the output to the inverting input. Find the transfer function Vout/Vin.
A 741 op-amp is used as a unity-gain voltage follower. Find the closed-loop -3 dB bandwidth.
A unity-gain Sallen-Key low-pass filter has R1 = R2 = 22 kOhm, C1 = 10 nF from the junction of R1 and R2 to the output and C2 = 4.7 nF from the non-inverting input to ground. Find f0 and Q.

An equal-component Sallen-Key high-pass filter uses C = 22 nF and R = 10 kOhm. Its gain is set by RA = 10 kOhm from the inverting input to ground and RB = 5.86 kOhm from the output to the inverting input. Find f0, Q and the pass-band gain.

A multiple-feedback low-pass filter has R1 = 10 kOhm from the input to node A, C1 = 47 nF from A to ground, R2 = 20 kOhm from A to the output, R3 = 10 kOhm from A to the inverting input and C2 = 4.7 nF from the inverting input to the output; the non-inverting input is grounded. Find the DC gain, f0 and Q.

A multiple-feedback band-pass filter has R1 = 15 kOhm from the input to node A, R2 = 1 kOhm from A to ground, C1 = 33 nF from A to the inverting input, C2 = 33 nF from A to the output and R3 = 300 kOhm from the inverting input to the output; the non-inverting input is grounded. Find the centre frequency, Q, the bandwidth and the gain at the centre frequency.

A unity-gain Sallen-Key low-pass filter has R1 = R2 = 10 kOhm, C1 = 22 nF from the junction of the resistors to the output and C2 = 11 nF from the non-inverting input to ground. Identify the type of response and find f0 and Q.
work: Q = sqrt(C1/C2)/2 = sqrt(2)/2 = 0.7071 (Butterworth); f0 = 1/(2 pi 1e4 sqrt(2.42e-16)) = 1023.1 Hz

question: An active first-order low-pass filter is an inverting amplifier with R1 = 10 kOhm at the input and Rf = 100 kOhm in parallel with Cf = 1.59 nF in the feedback path. Find the DC gain and the cutoff frequency.
work: K = -Rf/R1 = -10; fc = 1/(2 pi Rf Cf) = 1001 Hz

question: An active first-order high-pass filter has C1 = 100 nF in series with R1 = 1 kOhm from the input to the inverting input, Rf = 10 kOhm from the output to the inverting input and the non-inverting input grounded. Find the cutoff frequency and the high-frequency gain.
work: fc = 1/(2 pi R1 C1) = 1591.5 Hz; gain at high f = -Rf/R1 = -10
